stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan Alert: Atchanna orders steps for safety of farmers and fishermen
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan Alert: Atchanna orders steps for safety of farmers and fishermen
stories.summary: Puts officials on high alert to shield crops and fishermen from heavy rains and strong winds Nearly all fishing boats safely ashore; coastal paddy and horticulture under special focus
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: Agriculture and fisheries minister K Atchannaidu directed officials to remain on high alert and take precautionary measures to protect farmers, crops and fishermen in view of the heavy rains and strong winds forecast under Cyclone Akwan.
He stressed that the coalition government would stand by farmers and fishermen during the crisis.
As of November 14, kharif crops were standing on 21.32 lakh hectares and rabi crops covered 2.55 lakh hectares, taking the total cropped area to 23.87 lakh hectares.
Paddy accounted for 13.60 lakh hectares, red gram 4.42 lakh hectares and cotton 1.92 lakh hectares.
Special attention was directed towards 9.51 lakh hectares of crops in 10 coastal districts, including 9.16 lakh hectares of paddy.
Farmers were advised to harvest ready crops, clear field drains and avoid spraying fertilisers and pesticides during heavy rainfall.
Officials were also asked to protect 2,69,831 hectares of horticultural crops across 16 districts, including 1,08,615 hectares of chilli, 98,526 hectares of coconut and 24,469 hectares of turmeric.
Protective support should be provided to banana and papaya plants, while ready produce should be moved to markets.
The Minister said 30,635 of the 30,808 fishing boats had safely returned to shore by 10 am on November 16, while the remaining 173 boats were being monitored.
Around 1,08,250 voice alerts had been sent to fishermen, and 8,217 boats were being tracked through the Nabhimitra system.
Surveillance was intensified across 555 fishing villages and 350 landing centres.
Aquaculture farmers were advised to strengthen pond bunds and monitor water quality.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17
stories.summary: The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during this time
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal intensifying into cyclonic storm Akvan on Monday evening, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai has issued a cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts.
The cyclonic storm lay centred about 610 km east of Chennai at 5.30 p.m. on Monday (November 16, 2026).

The clouds associated with the system are likely to bring light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal, on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during the same period.

For Wednesday (November 18, 2026) and Thursday (November 19, 2026), the RMC has forecast that heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places over Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu districts.
The rain could be accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, with gusty winds reaching speeds of 40-50 km/hour at one or two places.
Heavy rain could occur at isolated places over Kancheepuram and Ranipet districts.
Moderate rain is likely to occur at a few places over the rest of north coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal.
Light rain may occur in isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places.
On Friday (November 20, 2026), moderate rain is likely in isolated places over the northern coastal districts of Tamil Nadu, the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal.
Light rain is likely at isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places.
It is very likely to continue moving north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening.

stories.headline: Kerala High Court refers petition challenging clean chit to Chief Minister in Punarjani case to Chief Justice
stories.title: Kerala High Court refers petition challenging clean chit to Chief Minister in Punarjani case to Chief Justice
stories.summary: High Court Registry directed to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: A Single Bench of the Kerala High Court has referred the petition challenging the closure of the preliminary inquiry against Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan in the Punarjani case for consideration before the appropriate court.
Justice C. Jayachandran observed that there was a strong prima facie indication that the petition had features of a public interest litigation (PIL).

The Bench directed the High Court Registry to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL.

The petition had been filed by lawyer K.M. Shajahan challenging a Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) report closing the preliminary inquiry and dropping corruption charges against the Chief Minister in connection with the Punarjani flood rehabilitation scheme.

The court examined two aspects while considering the petition — first, if the petitioner had the right to challenge the preliminary inquiry report, and second, if the court had the jurisdiction to hear the matter.
The petitioner argued that he had preferred the plea in his capacity as a citizen and a whistleblower, with every right to challenge the report.
The State pointed out that a petition in this regard was filed by one of the complainants in the Punarjani case.
This petition was later withdrawn and filed as a PIL seeking a CBI probe.
However, the PIL was dismissed by a Division Bench of the court.
The State contended that the petitioner did not have any right to move the petition since the complaint had already been decided by the court.
The Single Bench found that the jurisdiction to try the case would have to be decided first before examining the rights of the petitioner.

stories.headline: Tata Sons facing 'back-door takeover', warns Jimmy Tata
stories.title: Tata Sons facing 'back-door takeover', warns Jimmy Tata
stories.summary: Breaking his silence, Jimmy Tata, Ratan Tata's younger brother, has questioned developments that, in his view, could concentrate influence within a narrower group of trustees.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Jimmy has expressed his concerns in a note regarding what he described as a potential "back-door takeover" of Tata Sons, which is majority-owned by Tata Trusts, and questioned developments that, in his view, could concentrate influence within a narrower group of trustees.
, a trustee of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT).
It was this conversation that was recorded and later documented in a two-page note bearing the signatures of both.

However, the oldest member of the Tata family on the board of the trusts stopped short of indicating whether he would take a more active role, saying any future action would "depend on the situation".
The note argues that the induction of members of the Noel Tata family into the trusts was securing "a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlers' intention.

It is entirely inappropriate for more than one family member to serve on a given trust; doing so effectively confers ownership rights over the trusts' significant shareholding in Tata Sons at no consideration whatsoever."

The note also criticises amendments to Tata Sons' articles of association in 2013-14, saying they "fundamentally overturned" the earlier separation between the charitable trusts and Tata Sons' commercial operations by granting the Trusts' chairman veto powers and the ability to appoint directors.

The note further criticises the introduction of a "four-year time limit on the tenure of certain trustees while exempting others", arguing that it "compromised trustee independence and concentrated authority, enabling the marginalisation or removal of trustees who dissent." As an example, it cites the "targeting" of Venu Srinivasan "because he opposed the induction of Noel's son into the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, alongside the earlier removal of Vijay Singh for authoring a factual article." It also backs the continuation of Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran, noting that he had received "overwhelming support" and delivered record earnings and dividend payouts.

The note also argued that listing Tata Sons was "all the more critical" because it would "dismantle the pervasive culture of secrecy", impose greater accountability and increase scrutiny of the group's governance structure.
Jimmy's status as a perpetual trustee also places him at the centre of the governance discussion.
Apart from Jimmy, SRTT's perpetual trustees are Jehangir H C Jehangir and Noel.
